newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty slips as foreigners run from floods.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty slips as foreigners run from floods.

text.p: The zloty lost more than a figure in early Friday trade as foreign sales of Polish debt instruments intensified partly because of severe flooding in sourthern parts of the country, dealers said.
"Foreigners are selling zlotys partly because Poland is not in good condition with many parts of the country flooded," said Bogdan Stepkowski, senior dealer at ING Bank in Warsaw.

At 0830 GMT the zloty was at 0.25/0.14 percent above parity, down from opening's 0.54/0.47 and Thursday's close at 0.65/0.60. It was at 3.3200/40 to the dollar, against opening's 3.3080/00 and at 1.8900/15 per mark, against 1.8861/78.

The zloty was seen finding support at parity as some players expected the central bank to try to prop up the local currency with dollar- and mark-selling interventions if the zloty tried to break below parity.
Dealers said that movements in the Czech crown would closely be monitored on Friday, with any large-scale losses potentially sparking further position closing in Poland.
"If the crown declines in could take the zloty with it, just as it did in late May," one large Polish bank dealer said.
The crown weakend by nearly one percentage point to the mark on Friday following attacks on the currency from London.

The week-long flood, which put more than 300,000 hectares of southern Poland under water as well as large parts of the Czech Republic, prompted the Polish government to squeeze out 500 million zlotys from budget reserves to help flood victims.

Foreigners had been slowly pulling out of Polish treasuries over the last two weeks amid fears the country's booming domestic demand would not be restrained enough to avoid a Czech-style current account deficit crisis in future years.
On the money market one-day rates continued to straddle the three-day reverse repo rate of 22.45 percent without much impetus to edge higher or lower on Friday, dealers said.
At 0900 GMT overnight rates were at 22.25/22.50 percent against 22.30/22.50 at 0730 GMT and tomorrow/next were at 22.35/22.64 percent against 22.30/22.50.
